topIssues.title: kona/derive: derivation pipeline invariant analysis — bad L1 input must never halt derivation
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Invariant analysis of the kona derivation pipeline at `rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/`, mirroring the Go op-node analysis in #19491.

**Invariant**: No malformed or bad external input (batcher transactions, system config logs, deposit transactions from L1) should cause derivation to stop. Bad input should be dropped and processing should continue. Only logic errors are allowed to cause pipeline-halting (Critical) errors.

## Findings

All pipeline stages are correctly implemented **except for two issues**:

| Stage | File | Status |
|-------|------|--------|
| Traversal | `stages/traversal/` | ✅ System config errors ignored with warn |
| L1 Retrieval | `stages/l1_retrieval.rs` | ✅ |
| Frame Queue | `stages/frame_queue.rs` | ✅ Malformed frames silently dropped |
| Channel Bank | `stages/channel/channel_bank.rs` | ✅ |
| Channel Assembler | `stages/channel/channel_assembler.rs` | ✅ |
| Channel Reader | `stages/channel/channel_reader.rs` | ✅ |
| Batch Queue (pre-Holocene) | [`stages/batch/batch_queue.rs:388-390`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/48b31f0b1b1e9afcf4d07f75c28771f602cc6a1b/rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/stages/batch/batch_queue.rs#L388-L390) | ⚠️ See 19511 |
| Batch Stream (post-Holocene) | `stages/batch/batch_stream.rs` | ✅ |
| Attributes Builder | [`attributes/stateful.rs:114-120`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/48b31f0b1b1e9afcf4d07f75c28771f602cc6a1b/rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/attributes/stateful.rs#L114-L120) | ⚠️ See 19512 |
| Calldata Source | `sources/calldata.rs` | ✅ |
| Blob Source | `sources/blobs.rs` | ✅ |

## Sub-issues

- 19511 — `batch_queue.rs`: span batch extraction failure returns `Critical` instead of flushing and continuing
- 19512 — `stateful.rs`: system config update errors return `Critical` instead of being ignored

## Notes

- Deposit errors in `stateful.rs` returning `Critical` are **intentional** — matches Go op-node behaviour (deposits may never be silently dropped)
- `BatchValidity::Past` returning `Critical` pre-Holocene is **intentional** — should never be reached with valid external data

## Related

Companion to Go op-node analysis: #19491

---

topIssues.title: checkSpanBatch does not enforce activation-block user-tx rule that checkSingularBatch enforces
topIssues.author: trasnake87
topIssues.body:
`op-node/rollup/derive/batches.go` enforces the activation-block "no user transactions" rule (per spec [optimism/specs#791](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/791) and issue #17704) for singular batches but not for span batches. The same activation block, encoded as a span batch, is accepted.

### Where

`checkSingularBatch` (batches.go around L137) drops the batch:

```go
if (cfg.IsJovianActivationBlock(batch.Timestamp) ||
    cfg.IsKarstActivationBlock(batch.Timestamp) ||
    cfg.IsInteropActivationBlock(batch.Timestamp)) &&
    len(batch.Transactions) > 0 {
    log.Warn("dropping batch with user transactions in fork activation block")
    return BatchDrop
}
```

`checkSpanBatch` (batches.go L308–L445) validates timestamps, sequencer drift, deposit/SetCode tx exclusion per block, but never checks `IsJovianActivationBlock` / `IsKarstActivationBlock` / `IsInteropActivationBlock` against `batch.GetBlockTransactions(i)`.

History: PR #14797 added the rule for Isthmus (singular only, closed), PR #17984 added it for Jovian (singular only, merged), PR #19250 added Karst to the same condition (singular only, merged). PR #19150 separately added the SetCode check to span (`fix(op-node): add SetCodeTxType check to span batch validation`) — same kind of singular/span asymmetry, fixed in isolation. The activation-block rule appears to have been missed across all three iterations.

### Reproduction

A short unit test against `CheckBatch` builds the same activation-block user transaction twice — singular returns `BatchDrop`, span returns `BatchAccept`:

```go
package derive

import (
    "context"
    "math/big"
    "math/rand"
    "testing"

    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-core/forks"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-node/rollup"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/eth"
    "github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-service/testutils"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/common/hexutil"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/core/types"
    "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/log"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestSpanBatchActivationBlockUserTx(t *testing.T) {
    rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(0x51a75))
    chainID := big.NewInt(10)
    signer := types.NewLondonSigner(chainID)
    tx := testutils.RandomTx(rng, big.NewInt(1_000_000_000), signer)
    txData, err := tx.MarshalBinary()
    require.NoError(t, err)

    for _, fork := range []forks.Name{forks.Jovian, forks.Karst, forks.Interop} {
        t.Run(string(fork), func(t *testing.T) {
            l1A := eth.L1BlockRef{Hash: testutils.RandomHash(rng), Number: 100, Time: 1_000}
            l2Safe := eth.L2BlockRef{
                Hash: testutils.RandomHash(rng), Number: 200, Time: l1A.Time,
                L1Origin: l1A.ID(), ParentHash: testutils.RandomHash(rng),
            }
            cfg := &rollup.Config{
                Genesis:           rollup.Genesis{L2Time: l2Safe.Time},
                BlockTime:         2,
                SeqWindowSize:     4,
                MaxSequencerDrift: 30,
            }
            activationTime := l2Safe.Time + cfg.BlockTime
            cfg.ActivateAt(fork, activationTime)

            singular := &SingularBatch{
                ParentHash: l2Safe.Hash, EpochNum: rollup.Epoch(l1A.Number),
                EpochHash: l1A.Hash, Timestamp: activationTime,
                Transactions: []hexutil.Bytes{txData},
            }
            singularValidity := CheckBatch(context.Background(), cfg, log.New(),
                []eth.L1BlockRef{l1A}, l2Safe,
                &BatchWithL1InclusionBlock{L1InclusionBlock: l1A, Batch: singular}, nil)
            require.Equal(t, BatchValidity(BatchDrop), singularValidity)

            span := initializedSpanBatch([]*SingularBatch{{
                ParentHash: l2Safe.Hash, EpochNum: rollup.Epoch(l1A.Number),
                EpochHash: l1A.Hash, Timestamp: activationTime,
                Transactions: []hexutil.Bytes{txData},
            }}, cfg.Genesis.L2Time, chainID)

            spanValidity := CheckBatch(context.Background(), cfg, log.New(),
                []eth.L1BlockRef{l1A}, l2Safe,
                &BatchWithL1InclusionBlock{L1InclusionBlock: l1A, Batch: span}, nil)
            require.Equal(t, BatchValidity(BatchAccept), spanValidity,
                "span batches bypass activation-block user tx filtering")
        })
    }
}
```

`go test ./op-node/rollup/derive -run TestSpanBatchActivationBlockUserTx -v` passes for jovian, karst, and interop on `develop` (verified at `be742e31a`).

### Suggested fix

Apply the same condition inside `checkSpanBatch`'s per-block loop, before the per-tx validation:

```go
if (cfg.IsJovianActivationBlock(blockTimestamp) ||
    cfg.IsKarstActivationBlock(blockTimestamp) ||
    cfg.IsInteropActivationBlock(blockTimestamp)) &&
    len(batch.GetBlockTransactions(i)) > 0 {
    log.Warn("dropping span batch with user transactions in fork activation block")
    return BatchDrop
}
```

For symmetry with `checkSingularBatch` and consistency with the spec rule.

### Notes

The action test `TestActivationBlockTxOmission` added in #17984 uses `helpers.NewBatcherCfg()` which produces span batches by default (Delta+ fork, `ForceSubmitSingularBatch=false` → `useSpanChannelOut=true`). I have not run that test against current `develop`; if it currently passes, there is an additional path catching this that I have missed.

topPRs.title: op-private-interop,contracts!: derive and recover a private ETH chain public projection
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Private interop keeps application execution private while publishing the message history needed by the public interop set. One private-chain genesis produces a deterministic public projection, using standard span-batch transport and cross-chain dependency checks. This replaces #22729 and uses the existing `private-interop/devnet-readiness` branch unchanged at `9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2`.

Ordinary L1 deposits execute against private state. On the public projection, user deposits are included as successful no-ops with no minting, state changes, execution gas or logs; authenticated system deposits still execute. After sequencing-window expiry, interop invalidation or an L1 reorg, the private node returns to a surviving authenticated checkpoint and rebuilds canonical deposit-only intervals before publication resumes. Recovery ancestry persists across restarts, and batch publication waits for private reconciliation and an authorized batcher epoch.

The PoC remains operator-attested; execution-proof enforcement and private withdrawal settlement are future work. Native ETH bridge routes remain disabled in the private profile. The diff also includes the companion L1 event-certificate contracts, which are separate from the projection mechanism. Versioned bundle tooling, remote private-pair smoke, and deposit/recovery/reorg/rotation/cadence tests support devnet preparation.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** projection deposit execution, the claimed-follow RPC and recovery journal configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases when migrating from earlier prototypes. Configure the persistent recovery path and ordinary projection rollup RPC as documented in [DEVNET.md](https://github.com/karlfloersch/optimism/blob/9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2/op-private-interop/docs/DEVNET.md). Installing the custom native ETH bridge implementation requires explicit send/relay permissions.

Validation on this unchanged revision:

- Fourteen targeted Go test packages pass, covering private interop, batcher, claim-follow, chain container, driver, engine, sequencing, source client, smoke and devstack.
- Ten focused Rust projection/genesis tests and 78 targeted Solidity tests pass (Foundry lite profile). Main-workspace and SP1-guest Rust formatting pass.
- Full Go lint finds two existing issues: unchecked `big.Int.Uint64` in the position resolver and import ordering in the private interop preset. The fixes prepared locally are intentionally excluded to preserve this revision.
- Current upstream `develop` has three merge conflicts with this branch, in devstack configuration/signer setup. No upstream reconciliation is included.
- Full protocol/security review, full devnet acceptance and the production-cadence soak remain outstanding for this draft.

topPRs.title: feat: add private interop cleanroom implementation
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- add the private-interop private/rendering chain pair, contracts, deterministic rendering codec, builder, and claim-follow path
- integrate the pair with op-deployer, op-batcher, op-supernode, op-interop-filter, devstack, and op-up
- add private-pair-aware interop smoke coverage and a design document
- harden the implementation after adversarial review: structurally close deposits, bind rendering inputs and emitters, cap amplification, remove the separate operator key/premine, disable the stock ETH path, and make rendering execution fully zero-fee

## `op-up --private-interop` topology

```text
                         L1 EL + beacon node
                          ^              |
                          | batches      | derives
         +----------------+---+      +---v-----------------+
         |                    |      |                     |
   normal A batcher    private-interop batcher       shared supernode
         ^                    ^                      public view: {A, B-render}
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-node   B private op-node               |          |
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-reth   B private op-reth         A verifier   B rendering
   public chain 901    private chain 902           op-reth       op-reth
                              ^                                     |
                              +------ `/902/claimed` ----------------+
```

- Chain A is an ordinary public OP chain with a stock batcher and proposer.
- Chain B has two different histories sharing chain ID 902: the sequenced, user-facing custom-gas-token private chain and a public, derived-only rendering with no sequencer or mempool.
- The private-interop batcher reads private B blocks, converts exported logs into claim/replay transactions, checks the rendering parent, and posts an ordinary channel to L1.
- The shared supernode derives and judges `{A, B-render}` using the stock message database and cross-safety logic. It has no private-chain access and does not know that B is a rendering.
- The only private-interop addition in the supernode is the `/902/claimed` follow endpoint. It reconstructs the committed private-B safe block reference from public rendering claims for the private op-node; it does not alter judging.
- Private B and rendering B are never P2P-peered: they deliberately have the same chain ID but different genesis hashes and block contents.
- `--smoke` runs `interopsmoke` in the same process so private receipt positions can be resolved to their canonical public rendering positions.

## Verification

- `go test ./op-batcher/batcher ./op-chain-ops/interopsmoke/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state ./op-interop-filter/filter ./op-private-interop/... ./op-supernode/supernode/chain_container -count=1`
- focused op-deployer private-interop genesis/rollup integration tests
- 49/49 private-interop Solidity tests
- 24/24 L2-to-L2 messenger Solidity tests
- 15/15 L2 genesis Solidity tests
- `op-up --private-interop --smoke`: chain identity, native transfers, valid messages in both directions, rendered private-chain message resolution, and invalid-message reorg all pass

## Notes

This is intentionally a draft for design and security review. The stock Superchain ETH bridge smoke case is skipped on the custom-gas-token private half; that path is closed by design and `NativeMintBridge` is the sanctioned liquidity path.

topPRs.title: private-interop: derive public projection from one genesis
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This carries forward the private interop implementation from #22720, but replaces the draft's two-role/two-deployer genesis flow with one source of truth:

- op-deployer emits one private-chain genesis and rollup config; there is no public/rendering deployer role
- `ProjectGenesisFrom(privateChainGenesis)` is a pure, deterministic local transform with independent Go and Rust implementations and a shared cross-language golden vector
- op-reth accepts the same private genesis and applies the projection before database initialization with `--rollup.private[=true]`; the private EL consumes it unchanged
- op-batcher and op-supernode detect `private_interop` from the private rollup config, load the local private genesis, and derive the public projection automatically
- the projected state restores stock ETH semantics, installs the replay/claim predeploys, removes private-only liquidity/mint machinery, and clears only the private-chain feature bit
- private interop derives an L1 resource configuration with `maxResourceLimit = 0`, closing deposits through the stock portal rather than a custom L1 contract
- old role flags, compatibility paths, configurable projection predeploy addresses, and the second op-deployer run are deleted

The remainder of #22720 is retained: claim/replay contracts and codec, deterministic batch construction, claim-follow routing, interop-filter integration, devstack/op-up wiring, and acceptance coverage.

## Deployment shape

1. Run op-deployer once with the chain's `privateInterop` stanza and custom gas token configuration.
2. Give the emitted genesis to the private op-reth normally.
3. Give that same genesis to the public-projection op-reth with `--rollup.private=true`.
4. Give the private genesis path to op-batcher and op-supernode; their private-interop paths activate from the rollup marker and derive the matching projection locally.
5. Give the private LightCL the ordinary private-chain genesis/config. It follows the supernode's `/claimed` route as in #22720.

No projection step performs a network call. The embedded implementation bytecode is checked against the current contracts artifacts in the op-deployer integration test.

## Verification

- `go test ./op-private-interop/...`
- `go test ./op-batcher/batcher ./op-batcher/flags`
- `go test ./op-supernode/cmd ./op-supernode/supernode/...`
- `go test ./op-interop-filter/... ./op-node/rollup`
- focused op-deployer private-interop integration, pipeline, and state tests
- `go test ./op-devstack/sysgo -run '^$'`
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-chainspec private_interop` (4/4)
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node private` (1/1)
- `just lint` in contracts-bedrock
- messenger Solidity suite (24/24)

The broad op-deployer pipeline package also ran locally; its only failures were nine live-Sepolia tests that require `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`. The focused private-interop tests pass.

## Review note

A manual deletion/configuration review was completed, including a differential comparison against the retired two-deployer genesis path. Automated sub-agent review was unavailable in this harness.

topPRs.title: interop: suspend atomic demo router execution
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #22840. The atomic demo now supports nested cross-chain callbacks while retaining one live OP EVM transaction per chain. A on chain A calls B on chain B; B uses the same facade/router mechanism to call a distinct C on chain A; C sees A's pending state and can call back into the still-running B. The callback executes inside each chain's original transaction, preserving pending storage, transient storage, origin, gas ancestry and rollback. Each included chain receives one final replay after callback/result tapes and access lists are materialized; divergence rejects the candidate without discovery restarts or padding.

Canonical callback dispatch runs through ordinary router bytecode. Gas remains local to each chain: top-level application calls have fixed budgets, while callbacks receive half the remaining gas at their dispatch point. Caller context is restored on return, scheduling depth is capped at 32, and the bundle-wide call limit still applies. Failed callback hints force application rollback even if caught. ERC-4337 uses the existing EntryPoint and demo paymaster for normal on-chain gas settlement; it does not reimburse off-chain discovery or prove that a builder honestly attempted success. Existing Go and Kona cycle algorithms remain unchanged.

The Go/devstack bridge uses pinned candidate-prefix state and exact signed envelopes. This is a **demo node integration**; production payload-service admission/publication and a single-signature wallet flow remain out of scope. ETH forwarding, STATICCALL facades and committing after a caught remote failure remain unsupported. The original Go discovery path remains available for root-driven calls; nested dispatch is connected to the suspended builder.

Validation passed: all 18 contracts PR checks; full developer contract suite (2,290 passed, 183 skipped) and optimized suite (2,350 passed, 159 skipped); all 40 Rust builder tests with artifact-dependent tests enabled, including optimized bytecode; full Rust workspace lint/rustdoc and Go lint; Go bridge/message/filter/verifier tests; and Go/Kona nested-cycle regressions. All four real-node suspended/nested ERC-4337 success/revert cases pass, including exact receipt gas/log parity and sponsor settlement. Contract checks used the configured Foundry remappings plus explicit Solady/OpenZeppelin mappings with automatic remapping disabled to avoid the local duplicate `src/src` import issue.

Solidity, Rust lifecycle/application-effect and Go reviews are complete; all findings were fixed, none dismissed. Shared node fixtures are included by the normal contracts artifact build. #22840's branch remains unchanged.

CI on `ac7332b5d4af30420badf96e670243ec59df941d` is complete but not green: title/dependency checks and five Wiz scanners passed; Wiz SAST was skipped. The x86 multicannon package built, then [artifact attestation failed because the fork workflow lacks `id-token` permission](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/34524915489/job/103031802906), reproducing the previous head's permission failure. The other seven package jobs were canceled by fail-fast; image/smoke jobs were skipped. Full upstream CI for this fork still requires human authorization.

topPRs.title: kona: Add in-process zkVM canary for kona-sp1
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Overview

Adds `kona-zkvm-canary`, a long-running service that continuously executes the published Kona `super-range` guest against finalized live-network inputs using SP1’s CPU executor.

The canary executes both range and consolidation modes, compares their outputs with the native results produced during witness collection, and reports correctness failures without generating proofs or submitting work to the Succinct Prover Network.

This service is analogous to the vm-runner (op-challenger runner).

## What changed

- Added a finalized snapshot source that:
  - selects consecutive finalized timestamps;
  - pins L1 at `min(CurrentL1 - 1, L1 finalized)`;
  - validates super-root proofs, chain coverage, safety horizons, and span linkage;
  - resolves reported L1 identities against the configured L1 RPC;
  - classifies malformed or inconsistent parent data as `input_error`.
- Added in-process, sequential SP1 execution for range and consolidation modes.
- Added explicit SP1 cycle and memory limits.
  - Cycle-limit exhaustion is reported as `cycle_limit_exceeded`, never as a guest rejection.
  - The wall-clock deadline covers cancellable selection and witness stages only.
- Added fingerprint-based scheduling:
  - successful fingerprints are not rerun;
  - correctness failures receive one confirmation attempt;
  - attempts never overlap and cadence starts after completion.
- Added graceful shutdown during cancellable stages. A signal during uncancellable SP1 execution
  terminates the process and leaves restart handling to the orchestrator.
- Added startup artifact authentication:
  - loads `<prestate>.range.bin.gz`;
  - bounds compressed and decompressed sizes;
  - verifies the decompressed ELF SHA-256 and SP1 verification key;
  - keeps the authenticated ELF entirely in memory.
- Added structured, credential-redacted logging.
- Added Prometheus metrics for lifecycle, outcomes, target progress, stage durations, aggregate SP1 reports, artifact identity, and process memory.
  - Per-phase cycle and invocation totals remain in structured report logs rather than Prometheus series.
- Added `--once` for manual diagnostics using the normal execution path and existing `EXIT_VALID`, `EXIT_INVALID`, and `EXIT_INFRA` conventions.
- Added Melange/APKO packaging and image routing for a non-root, binary-only `kona-zkvm-canary` image. The guest ELF is not embedded in the image.
- Documented configuration, trust boundaries, execution bounds, metrics, and one-shot operation.

## Operational decisions

- Execution is in-process because SP1 already moves emulator work onto Tokio’s blocking pool.
- SP1 execution is not wrapped in a Tokio timeout because `spawn_blocking` work cannot be
  cancelled. The SP1 cycle limit is the resource-reclaiming execution bound.
- Finalized supernode responses are assumed immutable for a timestamp. The selected snapshot stays
  in memory for the attempt and is not fetched again after execution.
- The service writes no files. The sp1-sdk `TRACE_FILE` is rejected during configuration.
- Configuration and artifact authentication complete before the metrics listener is bound.
- `/health` comes from `kona-sp1-host-utils`; no readiness gauge or dedicated readiness behavior
  was added.
- No canary guest execution was added to CI, acceptance tests, or devstack.

Part of #18325
